opening.argument: The presentation describes Duanyam as a social enterprise built around women's skills, maternal and child health, and cultural promotion. It presents a concrete operating model: connecting artisans' existing skills to markets and supporting women's financial security, alongside baskets, slippers, trays, bags, wallets, and other woven products. The accompanying material identifies limited market access and sustainable natural resources as part of the context, while the speaker frames the discussion for people starting or running an early-stage business. Read together, this is an educational and operational account of craft production, market access, and entrepreneurship. It does not present a suspicious financial return, request private data, or promise a misleading benefit; the emphasis remains on ordinary products and the difficulty of building a business.
